title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy, mixed sets on Election Day as Apple wipes out and chips paddle back
conditions.summary: Futures are split: Nasdaq futures edge higher on a chip rebound while Dow futures slip on Apple's post-earnings drop. Midterm elections, Iran headlines and AMD's report after the close are the big swells today.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Around 5 AM Eastern, S&P 500 futures were flat, Nasdaq-100 futures rose about 0.5% and Dow futures fell about 0.4% (roughly 220 points); quotes are early and thin.
Monday's close: S&P 500 down 0.5%, Nasdaq-100 down 1.4% and now in correction territory, Dow up 0.4%.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.89%; the dollar index ended Monday near 101.8, with no fresh reading this morning.
WTI crude bounced about 1.6% to near $98 after Monday's roughly 8% plunge on Iran peace-talk hopes; gold slipped about 1.3% to near $3,917.
Bitcoin dipped about 1% to near $77,000 after roughly $399 million of spot bitcoin ETF outflows; the VIX sits near 21.
Asia was mixed: Korea's KOSPI fell more than 3% as Samsung and SK Hynix dropped about 5% on AI spending worries, while Australia rose 0.4% after the RBA hiked rates to 4.85%.
Europe was lower early on AI worries and Iran tensions after Monday's gains.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: Today is US midterm Election Day; polls favor Democrats to win the House while Senate control looks uncertain, and results start arriving tonight.
9:00 AM CT: JOLTS job openings for September, consensus about 7.1 to 7.2 million versus 7.08 million prior.
9:00 AM CT: Factory orders for September, consensus about +1.1% to +1.2% versus +0.1% prior, alongside revised durable goods.
Iran: talks with Washington continue with both sides citing progress, but the US struck Qeshm Island after Iran said it downed US drones near Hormuz.
No Fed speakers today; Fed officials speak Thursday and Friday ahead of Friday's October jobs report, where consensus is roughly +63,000 to +65,000 jobs.
Monday's ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 from 54.5, while September construction spending fell 1.9%.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Apple beat on revenue and earnings with strong iPhone sales, but missed on Greater China and warned rising memory-chip costs will squeeze holiday-quarter margins; shares are down about 4.5% pre-market.
Palantir beat and raised its full-year revenue outlook, with US commercial revenue topping government revenue for the first time, yet shares are down about 6% pre-market.
Before the open: Pfizer, Shopify, Eaton, Marathon Petroleum, Apollo, Archer-Daniels-Midland, Ferrari, Yum Brands and Keurig Dr Pepper; results were not out when this edition was prepared.
After the close: AMD is the headliner, plus Arista Networks, Super Micro Computer, Amgen, Booking Holdings, Block, AIG and Duolingo.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: AAPL (Apple): -4.5% — revenue beat, but China miss and a margin warning on memory costs.
PLTR (Palantir): -6.3% — beat-and-raise quarter not enough for a richly valued stock.
AEHR (Aehr Test Systems): +14.6% — raised its full-year revenue forecast.
HLIT (Harmonic): +16.1% — raised its full-year revenue forecast.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): +2.3% to +2.8% — chip rebound ahead of earnings tonight.
INTC (Intel): +2.4% — bouncing with chips after last week's guidance-driven slide.
NVDA (Nvidia): +1.6% — chip stocks recovering after Monday's Nasdaq selloff.

sections.title: Business News
items: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in a roughly $115 billion all-stock deal; both stocks fell sharply on Monday.
Oracle slid about 9% Monday after unveiling plans to raise about $20 billion in debt and equity to fund AI build-out.
China's regulator has paused large IPOs and big share sales, according to reports.
Australia's central bank raised rates a quarter point to 4.85% but signaled a softer path ahead.
Lower oil gave airlines a lift Monday while big oil producers slipped, as Iran diplomacy hopes swung crude.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 9:00 AM CT: JOLTS and factory orders, a read on the labor market ahead of Friday's payrolls.
After the close: AMD's results and data-center guidance, a key test for the battered AI chip trade.
Tonight: midterm results start rolling in from about 6 PM CT, with Iran headlines and crude near $100 in the background.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. It's Election Day, and my trusty co-anchor already cast his vote for more belly rubs. Gus the wonder dog, tell the folks good morning! Conditions today are fair, with choppy, mixed sets. Let's check the swell. In early, thin trading, S and P five hundred futures are flat. Nasdaq one hundred futures are up about half a percent. Dow futures are down about four tenths of a percent, around two hundred twenty points. Monday was gnarly for tech. The Nasdaq one hundred fell one point four percent and slipped into correction territory. The ten year Treasury yield eased to about four point eight nine percent. Crude oil bounced about one and a half percent to near ninety-eight dollars, after Monday's big wipeout on Iran peace talk hopes. Gold slipped about one percent. Bitcoin dipped about one percent, to near seventy-seven thousand dollars. The volatility index sits near twenty-one. In Asia, Korea dropped more than three percent on AI spending worries. Now the wind and weather. It's midterm Election Day, and results start rolling in tonight. At nine A M Central, we get job openings and factory orders. Iran talks continue, but there were fresh strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, so expect some gusts. Over on the tide chart, Apple beat on sales, but warned that rising memory chip costs will squeeze margins. Apple is down about four and a half percent before the bell. Even a Kahuna can wipe out. Palantir beat and raised its outlook, yet it's down about six percent. After the close, A M D is the big wave, along with Arista Networks, Super Micro, Amgen and Booking. In the lineup, Aehr Test Systems jumped about fifteen percent after raising its revenue forecast. Now that's catching a wave! That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Harmonic is up about sixteen percent on a forecast raise too. Chip makers like A M D, Intel and Nvidia are paddling back, up about two percent. On the beach, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal worth about one hundred fifteen billion dollars. Oracle plans to raise about twenty billion dollars to fund its AI build-out. And China paused big IPOs, so the grommets will have to wait. Sets to watch: the nine A M Central data, A M D tonight, and the election results. Soul surfers, stay patient and don't drop in on every headline. Want my read on any stock, E T F or futures contract?
